# NavigationFrame

Header: `winui/ui/navigation/NavigationFrame.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/navigation/NavigationFrame.hpp`.

A page host with a back and forward stack: shows one page at a time, built by a [PageFactory](#class-pagefactory) on each navigation, and animates between pages with a [NavigationTransition](../tree/element-transitions.md#struct-navigationtransition).

The frame owns the page on screen, and with NavigationCacheMode::Enabled also the cached pages on its stacks. [Layout](item-layouts.md#uilayout), input, focus and rendering pass straight through to the page on screen. While a transition plays, the leaving page is drawn under the arriving one and neither takes pointer input. The declarative form is [ui::NavigationFrame](#uinavigationframe), navigated through its `.control`.

Example: 
```cpp
auto frame_owned = std::make_unique<ui::NavigationFrameControl>();
frame_owned->set_content_transitions({ui::NavigationTransition{}});
frame_owned->on_navigated([](const ui::NavigationEventArgs& e) {
    if (e.mode == ui::NavigationMode::Back)
        std::println("came back");
});
ui::NavigationFrameControl* frame = window.set_content(std::move(frame_owned));

frame->navigate([] { return std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Home"); });
frame->navigate([] { return std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Settings"); },
                ui::ZoomPageTransition{});
if (frame->can_go_back())
    frame->go_back(); // "Home" again, rebuilt by its factory

// Or declaratively, taking the frame through .control:
ui::Control<ui::NavigationFrame> page_host;
window.set_content(ui::NavigationFrame{
    .content_transitions = {ui::NavigationTransition{}},
    .control             = page_host,
});
page_host->navigate([] { return ui::Text{.text = "Home"}; });
```

## `ui::NavigationFrame`

A page host with a back stack. Builds a [ui::NavigationFrameControl](#uinavigationframecontrol). The name [ui::Frame](../tree/namespace-ui.md#frame) belongs to the window's frame style. Navigate it through [`.control`](#uinavigationframe-control), since a page is a factory and navigation is an action on the frame.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Control<ui::NavigationFrame> frame;
ui::Property<bool>                back_enabled{false};

window.set_content(ui::NavigationFrame{
    .content_transitions = { ui::NavigationTransition{} },
    .on_navigated        = [&](const ui::NavigationEventArgs&) { back_enabled = frame->can_go_back(); },
    .control             = frame,
});
frame->navigate([] { return ui::Text{.text = "Home"}; });
frame->navigate([] { return ui::Text{.text = "Settings"}; }, ui::ZoomPageTransition{});
frame->go_back(); // "Home" again, rebuilt by its factory
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::NavigationFrame{
    .content_transitions, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height,
    .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .accessibility, .on_navigated, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus,
    .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

| <span id="uinavigationframe-on_navigated"></span>`on_navigated` | `ui::Callback<void(const ui::NavigationEventArgs&)>` |  | Called after the new page is in place. |
| <span id="uinavigationframe-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uinavigationframe-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uinavigationframe-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |

### build

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::NavigationFrameControl](#uinavigationframecontrol); the caller owns it.

## `ui::NavigationFrameControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

A page host with a back and forward stack: shows one page at a time, built by a [PageFactory](#class-pagefactory) on each navigation, and animates between pages with a [NavigationTransition](../tree/element-transitions.md#struct-navigationtransition).

The frame owns the page on screen, and with NavigationCacheMode::Enabled also the cached pages on its stacks. [Layout](item-layouts.md#uilayout), input, focus and rendering pass straight through to the page on screen. While a transition plays, the leaving page is drawn under the arriving one and neither takes pointer input. The declarative form is [ui::NavigationFrame](#uinavigationframe), navigated through its `.control`.

Example: 
```cpp
auto frame_owned = std::make_unique<ui::NavigationFrameControl>();
frame_owned->set_content_transitions({ui::NavigationTransition{}});
frame_owned->on_navigated([](const ui::NavigationEventArgs& e) {
    if (e.mode == ui::NavigationMode::Back)
        std::println("came back");
});
ui::NavigationFrameControl* frame = window.set_content(std::move(frame_owned));

frame->navigate([] { return std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Home"); });
frame->navigate([] { return std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Settings"); },

// Or declaratively, taking the frame through .control:
ui::Control<ui::NavigationFrame> page_host;
window.set_content(ui::NavigationFrame{
```

### NavigationFrameControl

```cpp
NavigationFrameControl() = default
```

An empty frame: no page, empty stacks, and no transitions (navigation is immediate).

### navigate

```cpp
bool navigate(PageFactory page, std::optional<PageTransition> transition = std::nullopt, NavigationCacheMode cache = NavigationCacheMode::Disabled)
```

Shows a new page, pushing the one on screen onto the back stack and clearing the forward stack. `transition` overrides the [NavigationTransition](../tree/element-transitions.md#struct-navigationtransition)'s default. Returns false and does nothing for an empty factory or one that builds nothing.

### go_back

```cpp
bool go_back(std::optional<PageTransition> transition = std::nullopt)
```

Moves the page on screen onto the forward stack, shows the top of the back stack and plays the transition backwards. The transition is the leaving entry's own unless `transition` is given. Returns false when the back stack is empty.

### go_forward

```cpp
bool go_forward()
```

Moves the page on screen back onto the back stack and shows the top of the forward stack, with the transition it was first navigated with. Returns false when the forward stack is empty.

### can_go_back

```cpp
bool can_go_back() const
```

Whether the back stack is not empty.

### can_go_forward

```cpp
bool can_go_forward() const
```

Whether the forward stack is not empty: a [go_back()](#go_back) has not been followed by a [navigate()](#navigate) since.

### back_stack_depth

```cpp
std::size_t back_stack_depth() const
```

How many pages [go_back()](#go_back) can return to.

### content

```cpp
Element* content() const
```

The page on screen, or nullptr before the first navigation.

### leaving

```cpp
Element* leaving() const
```

The page going away while its navigation transition plays, or nullptr.

### content_transitions

```cpp
const TransitionList& content_transitions() const
```

The transitions; a [NavigationTransition](../tree/element-transitions.md#struct-navigationtransition) here animates navigation.

### set_content_transitions

```cpp
void set_content_transitions(TransitionList transitions)
```

Replaces the transitions; takes effect from the next navigation.

### on_navigated

```cpp
void on_navigated(Callback<void(const NavigationEventArgs&)> handler)
```

Fired after the new page is in place, before it is laid out. A page's arrival work, like starting a connected animation, goes here.

### on_navigating_from

```cpp
void on_navigating_from(Callback<void(const NavigatingFromEventArgs&)> handler)
```

Fired before a navigation, with the page about to leave. The page is still on screen and laid out, so this is where to prepare a connected animation from it.

### for_each_child

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

Visits the page on screen only. A leaving page is never focusable, owns no popups and is not an automation child, and a [NativeControl](native-control.md#uinativecontrol) on a page left behind is hidden. clear_dirty() and [tick_override()](#tick_override) reach the leaving page too.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

The desired size of the page on screen, or zero with no page. The leaving page is measured too.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Both the page on screen and the leaving page fill the frame's whole rect.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

The leaving page, then the page on screen over it.

### clear_dirty_override

```cpp
void clear_dirty_override(DirtyFlags flags) override
```

Clears the frame's flags and those of both pages, the leaving one included.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Plays the leaving page's exit. Once it has finished, the page is destroyed, or kept on its stack entry if that entry caches it.

### class PageFactory

Derives from `ui::Callback< std::unique_ptr< Element >()>`.

Builds a page. Called on every navigation to it, and again on going back to it unless it was cached. A callable returning a `std::unique_ptr` to an [Element](../tree/element.md) works, and so does one returning a spec ([`[] { return ui::Text{.text = "Home"}; }`](text.md#uitext)), which is built each time.

#### PageFactory

```cpp
PageFactory() = default
```

No factory; [navigate()](#navigate) refuses it.

#### PageFactory

```cpp
template <typename F>
PageFactory(F page)
    requires std::invocable<F&> && (!std::convertible_to<std::invoke_result_t<F&>, std::unique_ptr<Element>>) && std::convertible_to<std::invoke_result_t<F&>, Spec>
```

A callable that returns a spec, built into the page on each call.

## struct NavigationEventArgs

What the frame's on_navigated() handler gets: the page now on screen, not laid out yet, and how it got there.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `Element*` | `nullptr` | The new page; owned by the frame, valid until it navigates away from it. |
| `mode` | `NavigationMode` | `NavigationMode::New` | Whether it arrived by navigate(), go_back() or go_forward(). |

## struct NavigatingFromEventArgs

What the frame's on_navigating_from() handler gets: the page about to leave, still on screen and laid out, and how the frame is leaving it.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | `Element&` |  | The page on screen now. |
| `mode` | `NavigationMode` | `NavigationMode::New` | Leaving by navigate(), go_back() or go_forward(). |

## Enumerations

### NavigationMode

```cpp
enum class NavigationMode
```

How the page on screen got there.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `New` | navigate(): a new page, the old one pushed onto the back stack. |
| `Back` | go_back(): the top of the back stack came back. |
| `Forward` | go_forward(): the top of the forward stack came back. |

### NavigationCacheMode

```cpp
enum class NavigationCacheMode
```

Whether a page on the back stack is kept alive (Enabled) or built again by its factory when it is gone back to (Disabled, the default).

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Disabled` | The page is destroyed when left and rebuilt by its factory on return. |
| `Enabled` | The page instance is kept on the stack and shown again as it was left. |
